sweet-potato.name: Kūmara
sweet-potato.summary: A starchy, sweet-tasting root vegetable native to tropical South America, a staple food in many regions and only distantly related to the true potato.

james-cook.name: James Cook
james-cook.summary: A British Royal Navy officer, explorer and cartographer (1728-1779) who led three Pacific voyages, completed the first European circumnavigation of New Zealand's main islands, and led the first European visits to eastern Australia and Hawaii.

ni-ihau.name: Ni'ihau
ni-ihau.summary: The seventh-largest and westernmost of the main Hawaiian islands, purchased by Elizabeth Sinclair in 1864 and known for preserving the Hawaiian language.

cook-islands.name: Cook Islands
cook-islands.summary: A self-governing Polynesian island nation in the South Pacific, in free association with New Zealand, made up of 15 islands with its capital at Avarua on Rarotonga.

mangaia.name: Mangaia
mangaia.summary: The southernmost and second-largest of the Cook Islands, once heavily populated but now much reduced after the decline of its pineapple industry.

george-vancouver.name: George Vancouver
george-vancouver.summary: Royal Navy officer and explorer (1757–1798) who charted North America's northwestern Pacific coast; Vancouver Island and the city of Vancouver are named after him.

kamehameha-i.name: Kamehameha I
kamehameha-i.summary: Conqueror and first ruler of the Kingdom of Hawaii, known as Kamehameha the Great, honored with a statue in the U.S. National Statuary Hall Collection.

makahiki.name: Makahiki
makahiki.summary: Ancient Hawaiian New Year festival honoring the god Lono, lasting four lunar months with feasting, rest, and a ban on labor and warfare.

sphingidae.name: Sphingidae
sphingidae.summary: A family of about 1,450 moth species, known as sphinx or hawk moths, admired for their fast, hummingbird-like hovering flight.

moai.name: Moai
moai.summary: Monolithic stone figures carved by the Rapa Nui people on Easter Island between 1250 and 1500, representing deified ancestors and set on platforms called ahu.

nan-madol.name: Nan Madol
nan-madol.summary: A lagoon city of artificial islets linked by canals on Pohnpei, capital of the Saudeleur dynasty until about 1628, later nicknamed the 'Venice of the Pacific.'

saudeleur-dynasty.name: Saudeleur dynasty
saudeleur-dynasty.summary: The first organized government to unite Pohnpei island, ruling from about 1100 to 1628 CE. Legend describes its rulers as foreign and increasingly oppressive, until they were overthrown by the invader Isokelekel.

pohnpei.name: Pohnpei
pohnpei.summary: The largest island of the Federated States of Micronesia, home to the megalithic ruined city of Nan Madol, begun in the 8th or 9th century.

temwen-island.name: Temwen Island
temwen-island.summary: A small island off Pohnpei in Micronesia, near the site of the ceremonial city of Nan Madol.

niutao.name: Niutao
niutao.summary: A reef island and district in the northern part of Tuvalu, with a population of about 550.

kealakekua-bay.name: Kealakekua Bay
kealakekua-bay.summary: A bay on Hawaiʻi Island's Kona coast, settled over a thousand years ago and home to ancient temples; it is the site where Captain Cook was killed in 1779.

john-young-advisor.name: John Young
john-young-advisor.summary: British subject (c. 1742–1835) who became a key military advisor to Kamehameha I in founding the Kingdom of Hawaii, and served as Royal Governor of Hawaii Island from 1802 to 1812.

isaac-davis-advisor.name: Isaac Davis
isaac-davis-advisor.summary: Welsh advisor to Kamehameha I who helped him conquer Hawaii's other kingdoms, arriving in 1790 as the sole survivor of a shipwreck massacre and later serving as a key advisor.

battle-of-nu-uanu.name: Battle of Nuʻuanu
battle-of-nu-uanu.summary: A May 1795 battle on Oʻahu, also called Kalelekaʻanae ('the leaping mullet'), in which King Kamehameha I's forces drove Oʻahu warriors off a cliff during his conquest of the Hawaiian Islands.

rongorongo.name: Rongorongo
rongorongo.summary: A system of glyphs found on Easter Island, discovered in the 19th century, that resembles writing but has never been deciphered; if genuine, it would be a rare independent invention of writing.

kumulipo.name: Kumulipo
kumulipo.summary: Hawaiian creation chant first recorded in the 18th century, including a genealogy of Hawaiian royalty, composed for Kalaninuiamamao and passed down to his daughter.

kalaninuiamamao.name: Kalaninuiamamao
kalaninuiamamao.summary: A Hawaiian prince and ancestor of Queen Liliuokalani, in whose honor the Kumulipo was composed before being passed down to his daughter.

hula.name: Hula kahiko
hula.summary: The ancient style of Hawaiian dance performed before Western contact, accompanied by chant and traditional instruments, distinct from the later Western-influenced 'auana style.

reimiro.name: Reimiro
reimiro.summary: A crescent-shaped wooden pectoral ornament worn by Easter Islanders, carved with a human face on each end and representing a Polynesian canoe.

alapa-iwahine.name: Alapaʻiwahine
alapa-iwahine.summary: Princess of the Island of Hawaii and great-grandmother of King David Kalākaua and Queen Liliʻuokalani, born of a rare father-daughter chiefly marriage.

lono.name: Lono
lono.summary: A Hawaiian god of fertility, agriculture, rain, music and peace, honored during the annual Makahiki festival.

kahuna.name: Kahuna
kahuna.summary: Hawaiian word for an expert in any field, historically used for priests, doctors, ministers and sorcerers.

tohunga.name: Tohunga
tohunga.summary: In Māori culture, an expert practitioner of a skill or art, such as a priest, healer, navigator, carver, or teacher, sometimes also a family head or chief.

whakapapa.name: Whakapapa
whakapapa.summary: The Māori concept of genealogy, central to identity, connecting people to land, ancestors, and tribal groups through recited lineages.

boustrophedon.name: Boustrophedon
boustrophedon.summary: A writing style in which alternate lines run in reverse, mirror-image directions, common on ancient Greek inscriptions and other early scripts.

felipe-gonz-lez-de-ahedo.name: Felipe González de Ahedo
felipe-gonz-lez-de-ahedo.summary: Spanish navigator and cartographer who commanded the 1770 Spanish expedition that landed on and formally annexed Easter Island for Spain.

paschalococos.name: Easter Island palm
paschalococos.summary: An extinct native palm species of Easter Island that vanished from the island's pollen record around 1650.

k-lauea.name: Kīlauea
k-lauea.summary: An active shield volcano on Hawaii Island, among the most active volcanoes on Earth, roughly 210,000 to 280,000 years old.

bay-of-plenty.name: Bay of Plenty
bay-of-plenty.summary: A large bay on New Zealand's North Island, named by James Cook in 1769 after seeing the abundant food at nearby Māori villages.

tu-i-kanokupolu.name: Tuʻi Kanokupolu
tu-i-kanokupolu.summary: A junior royal rank within Tonga's king's lineage, created to share regional rule, whose holders grew increasingly dominant over Tonga.

samuel-wallis.name: Samuel Wallis
samuel-wallis.summary: British Royal Navy officer and explorer (1728–1795) who made the first recorded European visit to Tahiti.

hms-dolphin-1751.name: HMS Dolphin
hms-dolphin-1751.summary: A Royal Navy frigate launched in 1751, the first ship to circumnavigate the globe twice, commanded successively by John Byron and Samuel Wallis.

matavai-bay.name: Matavai Bay
matavai-bay.summary: A bay on the north coast of Tahiti in French Polynesia, near the capital Pape'ete.

purea.name: Purea
purea.summary: A queen of the Landward Teva tribe of Tahiti (floruit 1769) who proclaimed herself ruler of all Tahiti and was encountered by early European expeditions.

tu-i-tonga.name: Tuʻi Tonga
tu-i-tonga.summary: A line of Tongan kings beginning in the 10th century with the mythical ʻAhoʻeitu, holding political power until yielding to the Tuʻi Haʻatakalaua in the 15th century; the title itself ended in 1865.

ferdinand-magellan.name: Ferdinand Magellan
ferdinand-magellan.summary: Portuguese explorer (c. 1480–1521) who led the Spanish expedition that made the first European crossing of the Pacific Ocean and reached the Philippines, where he was killed; his crew completed the first circumnavigation of the globe.

pedro-fernandes-de-queir-s.name: Pedro Fernandes de Queirós
pedro-fernandes-de-queir-s.summary: Portuguese navigator serving Spain (1563–1614), known for leading Pacific voyages, including the 1605–1606 expedition that searched for Terra Australis.

rakahanga.name: Rakahanga
rakahanga.summary: A small, remote atoll in the Cook Islands in the central-southern Pacific, with a population of 83 in 2016 and fully solar-powered electricity since 2014.

upolu.name: Upolu
upolu.summary: The most populous island of Samoa, home to the capital Apia, formed by a basaltic shield volcano and described as the first woman in Samoan mythology.

p-mare-dynasty.name: Pōmare dynasty
p-mare-dynasty.summary: The ruling family of the Kingdom of Tahiti from its unification in 1788 by Pōmare I until Pōmare V ceded the kingdom to France in 1880.

hms-bounty.name: HMS Bounty
hms-bounty.summary: A British Royal Navy ship sent to the Pacific in 1787 to collect breadfruit plants, made famous by the 1789 mutiny led by Fletcher Christian against Captain William Bligh.

kalani-pu-u.name: Kalaniʻōpuʻu
kalani-pu-u.summary: The supreme monarch (aliʻi nui) of the island of Hawaiʻi from about 1729 until his death in 1782, known to Europeans, through James Cook, as 'Terreeoboo, King of Owhyhee.'

k-wala.name: Kīwalaʻō
k-wala.summary: Aliʻi nui (paramount chief) of the island of Hawaii in 1782, defeated and overthrown by Kamehameha I at the Battle of Mokuohai.

battle-of-moku-hai.name: Battle of Mokuʻōhai
battle-of-moku-hai.summary: An 1782 battle on Hawaiʻi Island and Kamehameha I's first major victory in his wars to conquer the Hawaiian Islands.

willem-schouten.name: Willem Schouten
willem-schouten.summary: Dutch navigator (c. 1567–1625) for the Dutch East India Company, the first to sail the Cape Horn route into the Pacific Ocean.

jacob-le-maire.name: Jacob Le Maire
jacob-le-maire.summary: A Dutch mariner who circumnavigated the Earth in 1615–1616, during which the strait between Tierra del Fuego and Isla de los Estados was named for him, shortly before his expedition rounded Cape Horn and proved Tierra del Fuego was not a continent.

niuatoputapu.name: Niuatoputapu
niuatoputapu.summary: A volcanic island in the north of Tonga, in the Pacific Ocean, whose name means "sacred island."

abel-tasman.name: Abel Tasman
abel-tasman.summary: Dutch seafarer employed by the Dutch East India Company who in 1642 became the first European to reach New Zealand and Tasmania, naming the latter Van Diemen's Land after his patron.

louis-antoine-de-bougainville.name: Louis-Antoine de Bougainville
louis-antoine-de-bougainville.summary: A French naval officer and explorer (1729–1811) who circumnavigated the globe in 1763, made the first recorded settlement on the Falkland Islands, and voyaged into the Pacific.

french-frigate-boudeuse.name: Boudeuse
french-frigate-boudeuse.summary: A 32-gun French sailing frigate, famous as Louis Antoine de Bougainville's exploration ship from 1766 to 1769, later serving in Revolutionary-era wars.

juan-sebasti-n-elcano.name: Juan Sebastián Elcano
juan-sebasti-n-elcano.summary: A Spanish navigator (1486/87–1526) who completed the first circumnavigation of the Earth after Magellan's death, by continuing the voyage westward across the Indian Ocean.

k-ne.name: Kāne
k-ne.summary: The highest of the three major Hawaiian deities, worshipped as the god of procreation, creator of life, and ancestor of chiefs and commoners, associated with dawn, sun and sky.

k.name: Kū
k.summary: One of the four great gods of Hawaiian religion, worshiped under many names including Kūkāʻilimoku, whose rites uniquely included human sacrifice.

kanaloa.name: Kanaloa
kanaloa.summary: A Hawaiian god symbolized by the squid or octopus, associated with the ocean and seamanship, and traditionally paired with the god Kāne.

mililani-trask.name: Mililani Trask
mililani-trask.summary: Leader of the Hawaiian sovereignty movement, attorney and political speaker who founded Na Koa Ikaika o Ka Lāhui Hawaiʻi and helped author the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples.

tikopia.name: Tikopia
tikopia.summary: A remote, culturally Polynesian volcanic island in the Solomon Islands, noted as one of the most thoroughly documented small-scale societies.

rarotonga.name: Rarotonga
rarotonga.summary: Largest and most populous island of the Cook Islands, home to about 72% of the country's population and its capital, Avarua.

aumakua.name: ʻAumakua
aumakua.summary: In Hawaiian belief, a personal or family guardian spirit descended from a deified ancestor, often taking the form of an animal such as a shark or owl.

laka.name: Laka
laka.summary: A hero figure in Hawaiian mythology, known elsewhere in Polynesia as Rata or Lata, tied to a legend of avenging his father's murder.

papah-naumoku.name: Papahānaumoku
papah-naumoku.summary: The Earth Mother goddess in ancient Hawaiian mythology, consort of the sky god Wākea, still worshipped by some Hawaiians as a primordial creative and healing force.

pele-deity.name: Pele
pele-deity.summary: Hawaiian goddess of volcanoes and fire, said to have created the Hawaiian Islands and still a prominent figure in Hawaiian mythology and culture.

ho-oponopono.name: Hoʻoponopono
ho-oponopono.summary: A traditional Hawaiian practice of reconciliation and forgiveness, meaning 'correction'; similar forgiveness practices exist elsewhere in the South Pacific.

heiau.name: Heiau
heiau.summary: A Hawaiian temple built in styles ranging from earth terraces to stone platforms, used for purposes from healing to war; some were dedicated through human sacrifice.

ali-i.name: Aliʻi
ali-i.summary: Traditional hereditary nobility of the Hawaiian islands, spanning several ranks of chiefs that could be held by men or women.

native-hawaiians.name: Kanaka Maoli
native-hawaiians.summary: Indigenous Polynesian people of the Hawaiian Islands, settled at least 800 years ago, who developed a distinct culture and formed the Hawaiian Kingdom in 1795 under Kamehameha the Great.
